items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We had Minor Hall on drums... and myself on bass, and King Oliver was playing. That's the way the band was picked up when we went to Frisco

ctx.x: David Jones playing alto, mellophone and sax. We had Johnny Dots playing clarinet. We had Lilian Armstrong on piano. We had Minor Hall on drums, and we had Notre Dutre on trombone, and myself on bass, and King Oliver was playing. That's the way the band was picked up when we went to Frisco, playing at the Procola dance hall.
And when you came west, did you plan to stay here, or did you just come for a short trip? Well, we come to play that engagement, that's all.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: I'll start with Buster Wilson on the piano. Joe Dorersbourg on clarinet. Papa Mutt [Carey] on the trumpet. Ram Hall on the drums. ... During that time, who did I have in that band. Lloyd Glenn, Joe, ah, Ram, myself, Buster Wilson

ctx.x: He played violin. Also clarinet. And Joe let him go. So this boy Minor Hall, we called him Ram, said, 'Well, why are you going to fire this man? We're at the end of the Southern Pacific Line and (Unintelligible). He said, 'I've got a lot to do with it. I don't think it's right.' Then he said, 'Well, if that's the case, I'll go too.'

That was the drummer, (Unintelligible). So finally, he went to the union and told them about it -- number six -- and said, "Did you get a notice?" And he said, "No." "Did you give him a notice?" He said, "No." And they said, "Well, he done sent for another drummer trombonist." He said, "What?" He sent for Baby Davey Dodds. He's in St. Louis. Baby Davey Dodd's coming in from St. Louis and (Unintelligible). So they called in Joe and Joe -- told Joe he had to pay Jimmy -- give Jimmy two weeks, pay Jimmy for two…
